title_en: Li Shuaishuai v. Shanghai General Fuji Refrigeration Co., Ltd. and Shanghai Industrial and Commercial Information School — dispute over compensation for personal injury
ruling_gist_en: 1. Where an intern sustains injury due to work-related reasons during working hours and at the workplace while working at the internship unit, even if the intern has general fault, the liability for compensation of the internship unit shall not be reduced.
keywords_en: civil; dispute over compensation for personal injury; first instance; basic people's court; Shanghai; natural person; legal person; Civil Code; liability for injury of intern during work; school's safety guarantee obligation to interns; calculation standard for disability compensation for students with rural household registration; partial support; intern; injury from operating machinery; finger amputation; level 9 disability; compensation for personal injury; traffic accident; personal injury compensation dispute of Information School
full_text_en:
Li Shuaishuai v. Shanghai General Fuji Refrigeration Co., Ltd. and Shanghai Industry and Commerce Information School — Dispute over Compensation for Personal Injury

Ruling Summary

1. Where an intern is injured during work at the internship unit, during work hours and at the work site, due to work-related reasons, even if the intern is at general fault, such fault shall not reduce the internship unit's liability for compensation.

2. A school shall, in accordance with law, provide necessary safeguards for the intern's safety precautions and rights and interests during the internship. If the school fails to exercise the necessary supervisory obligations over the internship unit, it shall bear corresponding legal liability for the intern's injury consequences according to the degree of its fault.

3. For a student with rural household registration who is enrolled in an urban primary or secondary school and is injured or disabled during the school's educational or teaching activities (including dispatched internships), the disability compensation shall be calculated based on the urban resident standard of the locality where the school is located.

Plaintiff: Li Shuaishuai, male, 20 years old, Han ethnicity, domiciled in Pingchang County, Sichuan Province.

Defendant: Shanghai General Fuji Refrigeration Co., Ltd., domiciled at Songze Avenue, Qingpu District, Shanghai.

Legal Representative: Chen Yabiao, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Defendant: Shanghai Industry and Commerce Information School, domiciled at Gongyuan East Road, Qingpu District, Shanghai.

Legal Representative: Fang Deming, Principal of the school.

The plaintiff, Li Shuaishuai, filed an action with the Qingpu District People's Court of Shanghai against the defendants, Shanghai General Fuji Refrigeration Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "General Fuji Company") and Shanghai Industry and Commerce Information School (hereinafter "Commerce School"), concerning a dispute over liability for harm to a service provider.

Plaintiff's Allegations: On July 8, 2013, the plaintiff was arranged by the defendant Commerce School to intern at the defendant General Fuji Company. At approximately 11:00 a.m. on November 2, 2013, mechanical equipment at the internship site crushed the plaintiff's right hand, causing complete severance of the second through fifth fingers of the right hand. After treatment, the index and middle fingers were reattached. Forensic appraisal determined that the plaintiff's right hand disability was equivalent to a Class IX disability under road traffic accident standards. Therefore, the plaintiff filed this lawsuit, requesting the court to order the two defendants to compensate the plaintiff for: nursing expenses of RMB 5,460 (calculated at RMB 1,820 per month for 3 months); lost income of RMB 24,200 (calculated at RMB 3,000 per month for 242 days); nutrition expenses of RMB 2,400 (calculated at RMB 40 per day for 60 days); hospital meal subsidies of RMB 1,380 (calculated at RMB 20 per day for 69 days); disability compensation of RMB 175,404 (calculated at the Shanghai urban resident standard of RMB 43,851 per year for 20 years with a coefficient of 0.2); moral damages of RMB 10,000; appraisal fees of RMB 1,800; attorney's fees of RMB 5,000; and transportation expenses of RMB 500, totaling RMB 226,144.

Defendant General Fuji Company's Defense: It expressed apology for the accident involving the plaintiff Li Shuaishuai at its company and indicated willingness to provide compensation within the scope of the law. It had no objection to the facts, but the direct cause of the plaintiff's injury was his operational error — failing to cut off the power when changing the mold. After the accident, General Fuji Company promptly sent the plaintiff to the hospital for treatment and paid medical expenses of RMB 71,718.60, nursing expenses of RMB 2,040, nursing supplies of RMB 180, and accommodation expenses for the plaintiff's family of RMB 800. In addition, it paid RMB 4,000 in advance to the plaintiff's family, which should be addressed together in this case. Regarding nursing expenses and hospital meal subsidies, the relevant costs had already been directly borne by General Fuji Company, so they were duplicative. As for lost income, the plaintiff was a student, so there was no such thing as lost income; during the internship, he only received a monthly internship subsidy of RMB 1,800. The nutrition expenses of RMB 40 per day were excessive. Regarding disability compensation, the plaintiff had rural household registration and did not provide evidence that he met the conditions for applying the urban household standard, so it should be calculated according to the rural standard. Transportation expenses should be calculated based on actual expenses incurred. It had no objection to the moral damages, attorney's fees, and appraisal fees. All expenses should be apportioned according to the liability ratio of the parties.

Defendant Commerce School's Defense: It had no objection to the facts of the plaintiff Li Shuaishuai's injury. The various expenses should be adjudicated in accordance with the law, and it agreed with the defendant General Fuji Company's opinion on the expenses.

Facts Found by the Court at First Instance (Qingpu District People's Court of Shanghai):

The plaintiff Li Shuaishuai was a student in the 2011 class of the mold profession at the defendant Commerce School. On July 8, 2013, Li Shuaishuai, the Commerce School, and the defendant General Fuji Company signed a "Student Internship Agreement," stipulating that after a mutual selection between Li Shuaishuai and General Fuji Company, Li voluntarily chose to intern at General Fuji Company for a period from July 8, 2013, to June 25, 2014. During the internship, General Fuji Company would pay Li an internship subsidy of RMB 1,800 to 2,000 per month based on no more than 40 hours per week as prescribed by the state, and overtime exceeding the prescribed time, as well as mid-shifts, night shifts, and special positions required by work, would be compensated on the same basis as General Fuji Company's regular employees. Before assigning interns to work, General Fuji Company should first provide training and education on corporate culture, job requirements, professional skills, operational standards, production safety, and labor discipline, assign them to departments and positions that conform to national labor protection laws and regulations and are free from harm to the person and adverse effects on the physical and mental health of young people, and designate a mentoring master to provide guidance and evaluation during the internship. For internship positions prone to accidental occupational injuries, General Fuji Company should, in addition to strengthening production safety education before the intern begins work, provide appropriate labor protection measures. The school would purchase "Student Internship Liability Insurance" for the intern. The agreement also contained other provisions.

At approximately 11:00 a.m. on November 2, 2013, the plaintiff Li Shuaishuai was working overtime at the defendant General Fuji Company operating a CNC bending machine. While changing the mold, he accidentally stepped on the switch, causing the machine to sever the second through fifth fingers of his right hand. Li Shuaishuai was immediately sent to the Shanghai Sixth People's Hospital for emergency treatment, then admitted the next day for finger replantation surgery. On November 14, 2013, he was transferred to Shanghai Songjiang District Jiuting Hospital for debridement and revision amputation of the ring and little fingers, and was discharged on January 10, 2014. He subsequently received multiple outpatient treatments. As of March 5, 2014, Li Shuaishuai had incurred total medical expenses of RMB 88,001.76 (including meal expenses of RMB 855, of which RMB 16,283.25 was paid by the children's medical insurance). On October 9, 2014, as commissioned by the court, the Judicial Appraisal Center of the Institute of Forensic Science issued an appraisal opinion on Li Shuaishuai's injuries: The injury to his right hand and other parts resulted in residual functional impairment of the right hand, equivalent to a Class IX disability under road traffic accident standards, with a rest period of 150–180 days, nursing period of 90 days, and nutrition period of 60 days. Li Shuaishuai incurred appraisal fees of RMB 1,800 for this. He also incurred attorney's fees of RMB 5,000.

After the incident, the defendant General Fuji Company paid on behalf of the plaintiff Li Shuaishuai: medical expenses of RMB 71,718.51, nursing expenses of RMB 2,040, daily necessities of RMB 180, accommodation expenses for Li's family of RMB 800, and also paid RMB 4,000 in cash to Li's family, totaling RMB 78,738.51.

It was also found that the plaintiff Li Shuaishuai had an agricultural household registration.

During the first-instance trial, the plaintiff Li Shuaishuai stated that before the internship, the defendant Commerce School had provided him with safety education and training, and the defendant General Fuji Company had also provided pre-job training. He was issued labor protection gloves. He had been operating the bending machine since August 2013. The night before the incident was a Friday; Li was on the night shift. Because General Fuji Company required overtime on Saturday, Li chose to continue working the early shift on Saturday. However, his mentoring master was not working overtime, so Li operated the bending machine on his own. There were other shift leaders at General Fuji Company who could provide guidance. Normally, the mold should have been changed by the shift leader, but after using the restroom, Li was in a hurry to return and change the mold to continue working, so he tried to change the mold himself and then find another shift leader to help adjust the mode. In the process of changing the mold, he accidentally stepped on the switch, and the upward movement of the mold crushed his fingers. Normally, when the master needed to change the work mode, he would cut off the power, adjust the mode, and then change the mold. Li considered himself unable to operate the machine independently. General Fuji Company stated that Li was able to independently perform simple operations at the time of the injury and that having other shift leaders present was equivalent to having the master provide guidance. Commerce School argued that it was unclear whether Li could operate independently and that Commerce School did have an obligation to ensure Li's safety. Commerce School claimed it was unclear whether Li could operate independently. Commerce School stated it was indeed obligated to ensure Li's safety.

Judgment of the First Instance Court (Qingpu District People's Court of Shanghai):

The court held that the defendant General Fuji Company, as the internship unit, was the provider of the intern's labor tools and the director of the work content, and bore the duty of daily management and protection of the intern, as well as the necessary safety protection obligations. Since the work equipment provided by General Fuji Company had a certain degree of danger, requiring the plaintiff Li Shuaishuai to operate the machine during the internship without arranging a mentoring master to provide guidance at his side constituted fault for Li's injury. Li, as an adult with full civil capacity, who had undergone relevant professional knowledge learning and internship training, should have had a certain awareness of the danger of operating the equipment. As an intern engaged in internship labor, Li should also have exercised necessary caution. However, Li changed the mold himself without the guidance of a mentoring master and failed to follow correct operating procedures, failing to exercise due care, and thus bore some fault for the occurrence of the damage. The existing evidence was insufficient to prove that the defendant Commerce School was at fault in this accident, so Li's claim for compensation for damages against Commerce School was difficult to support. Taking into account the circumstances of the case, the first-instance court confirmed that General Fuji Company should bear 80% of the liability for the economic losses caused by Li's injury, and Li should bear 20% of the liability himself. The losses of Li Shuaishuai were calculated as follows: 1. Medical expenses: based on the receipts, RMB 88,001.76, of which meal expenses of RMB 855 and the children's medical insurance payment of RMB 16,283.25 should be deducted, leaving RMB 70,863.51, which was confirmed. 2. Hospital meal subsidies: RMB 1,380; nursing expenses: RMB 5,460; moral damages: RMB 10,000; Li's calculations complied with the law and were confirmed. 3. Nutrition expenses: based on the circumstances, discretionarily confirmed at RMB 30 per day for the 60 days determined by the appraisal, totaling RMB 1,800. 4. Lost income: based on the internship agreement between Li and General Fuji Company, discretionarily confirmed at RMB 1,820 per month for 6 months, totaling RMB 10,920. 5. Disability compensation: Li had agricultural household registration and did not provide evidence that he had lived in an urban area and relied on urban income as his main source of living for more than one year; therefore, it should be calculated according to the Shanghai rural population standard of RMB 19,208 per year for 4 years, totaling RMB 76,832. 6. Transportation expenses: based on the circumstances, discretionarily confirmed at RMB 300. 7. Appraisal fees: RMB 1,800, confirmed. 8. Daily necessities: RMB 180; accommodation expenses: RMB 800; these were actual expenses incurred by Li and his family due to Li's injury, both parties acknowledged them, and General Fuji Company had fully paid them, so they were confirmed. 9. Attorney's fees: RMB 5,000, which were the actual expenses incurred by Li for this lawsuit, and both General Fuji Company and Commerce School acknowledged them, so they were confirmed. In summary, Li's losses (excluding attorney's fees) totaled RMB 180,335.51, of which General Fuji Company should bear 80%, i.e., RMB 144,268.41, plus attorney's fees totaling RMB 149,268.41. After deducting the medical expenses, nursing expenses, daily necessities, accommodation expenses, and advance cash already paid by General Fuji Company totaling RMB 78,738.51, General Fuji Company should still pay Li the remaining amount of RMB 70,529.90.

In conclusion, the Qingpu District People's Court of Shanghai, in accordance with Article 98 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 6 (1), Article 15 (1)(vi), Articles 16, 22, and 26 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, and 25 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Personal Injury Compensation Cases, and Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Actions, rendered judgment on March 30, 2015:

1. Shanghai General Fuji Refrigeration Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate Li Shuaishuai for the economic losses caused by this injury, totaling RMB 70,529.90;

2. All other claims of Li Shuaishuai are dismissed.

Li Shuaishuai appealed against the first-instance judgment to the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, alleging: As an intern, Li was under the dual management of the appellees Commerce School and General Fuji Company. General Fuji Company arranged for Li to work overtime on the Saturday in question without a mentoring master accompanying him, even though Li had been on the night shift the previous day. Both Commerce School and General Fuji Company were responsible for Li's injury. Li was a student at Commerce School, which is located at Gongyuan East Road, Qingpu District, Shanghai, so Li's disability compensation should apply the Shanghai urban resident standard. Lost income should be calculated based on Li's actual internship income of RMB 3,000 per month, and the lost income period should include Li's 69-day hospitalization. Therefore, Li requested the appellate court to set aside the first-instance judgment and support all claims made by the appellant in the original trial.

The appellee General Fuji Company argued: The appellant Li Shuaishuai was an intern with no fixed working hours. The day of the incident was Saturday, and the mentoring master was not working; Li chose to work overtime on his own. There were shift leaders present, and Li could have consulted them. Li was at fault for the accident. General Fuji Company had provided him with pre-job training and issued labor gloves, and had actively treated him after the incident, thus fulfilling its obligations. The appellee Commerce School also had certain safety protection obligations towards Li and should bear corresponding liability. Li's disability compensation should be calculated based on his household registration type, and his lost income should be calculated based on the internship subsidy of RMB 1,800 per month. It requested the appellate court to dismiss the appeal and uphold the original judgment.

The appellee Commerce School argued: According to relevant regulations, during the internship of vocational school students, internship units shall not arrange overtime. Commerce School also emphasized to the internship enterprise that interns should not be arranged to work overtime. It requested the appellate court to adjudicate in accordance with the law.

Findings of the Second Instance Court (Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court):

After the second instance, the court confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

Reasoning of the Second Instance Court:

In this case, the appellant Li Shuaishuai, as a student of a secondary vocational school, interned at General Fuji Company after signing the "Student Internship Agreement" with the appellees Commerce School and General Fuji Company. The three parties in this legal relationship were bound not only by the agreement but also by the relevant laws and regulations concerning internships for secondary vocational school students. The "Measures for the Management of Internships for Secondary Vocational School Students" jointly issued by the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Finance, as well as the "Notice of the General Office of the Ministry of Education on Addressing the Enterprise Skilled Worker Shortage and Further Improving Internship Work for Secondary Vocational School Students," provide that schools and relevant enterprises "shall not arrange for students to engage in on-the-job internships exceeding 8 hours per day; shall not arrange overtime for students." Although such regulatory documents of State Council departments are not directly applicable as legal bases for court judgments, they may serve as a basis for the court to assess whether the school was at fault in this case. In this case, based on the consistent confirmation of the three parties at trial, Li was indeed working overtime on Saturday at the time of the incident, and the mentoring master did not accompany him during overtime. For the injury suffered by Li during this overtime work while operating dangerous work equipment, the liability of each party is as follows:

First, the appellee General Fuji Company, as the direct manager of the appellant Li Shuaishuai during the internship, could direct and arrange how Li performed his internship work and could supervise and manage the work process. Although Li was an intern, the labor he performed objectively created economic benefits for General Fuji Company. Li still enjoyed the right to labor protection, and the source of danger that caused Li's injury fell within the normal risk scope of the labor he was performing. Therefore, considering comprehensively the relationship of direction and control between General Fuji Company and Li, the attribution of economic benefits created by the labor, the labor protection duties and responsibilities for controlling and preventing labor risks that General Fuji Company should bear, General Fuji Company should bear the primary liability for the damage suffered by Li in this case.

Second, the appellee Commerce School, as the indirect manager of Li during the internship, should provide necessary safeguards for the student's safety precautions and rights and interests during the internship in accordance with law. Although Commerce School could not directly direct Li's work, as a vocational education institution, it should have been aware of the dangers of student participation in internship work. It should have controlled and prevented risks through safety education for students and communication and negotiation with the enterprise. However, despite being aware of the relevant regulations that internship units shall not arrange overtime for interns, Commerce School failed to take preventive measures such as strengthening safety education for students and clearly stipulating with the enterprise, and in fact allowed the existence of overtime for interns. Therefore, Commerce School failed to fulfill its duty of prevention and supervision. Considering that Commerce School could not directly direct Li's specific work at General Fuji Company, Commerce School should bear secondary liability for the damage suffered by Li.

Finally, the appellant Li Shuaishuai, as an intern, was still at the learning stage in terms of skills, and his labor remuneration was different from that of the appellee General Fuji Company's regular employees. Therefore, the standard of care and attention Li should have exercised in the labor process should not be equated with that of General Fuji Company's regular employees. The operational error committed by Li on the day of the incident, when there was no mentoring master accompanying him during overtime, did not constitute gross negligence. Compared with the risk prevention obligations that General Fuji Company and Commerce School should have assumed, Li's own general fault should not reduce the compensation liability that General Fuji Company and Commerce School should bear. Moreover, where a regular employee with an established labor relationship suffers a similar work-related injury due to his own fault, the worker's compensation he can receive is not reduced due to his own fault. Therefore, for Li, who was still an intern, his own general fault should not reduce the compensation liability of the relevant tortfeasors. Consequently, the first-instance court's requirement that Li bear 20% of the personal injury losses himself was inappropriate. Given that Commerce School had some fault in this case, the first-instance judgment ordering General Fuji Company to bear 80% of the liability for the damage consequences was proper. The remaining 20% of the liability should be borne by Commerce School. The second instance hereby modifies the judgment accordingly.

Furthermore, regarding the calculation standard for disability compensation, according to Article 20 of the *Regulations of Shanghai Municipality on the Handling of Student Injury Accidents in Primary and Secondary Schools*: "Disability compensation. It shall be calculated based on the disability grade of the injured student, at the standard of the per capita disposable income of urban residents in the municipality for the previous year, for a period of 20 years from the date of disability confirmation." Furthermore, according to Article 2 of the said *Regulations*, these *Regulations* apply to personal injury accidents involving primary and secondary school students occurring during educational and teaching activities at primary and secondary schools in Shanghai Municipality, and do not distinguish whether the injured student is a Shanghai resident or a non-Shanghai resident, nor whether they hold urban or rural household registration. Therefore, they shall apply to all students enrolled in Shanghai primary and secondary schools. As secondary vocational schools fall within the category of secondary schools, and assigning internships constitutes part of educational and teaching activities, the said *Regulations* shall also apply to student injury accidents during internships assigned by Shanghai secondary vocational schools. In this case, at the time of the incident, the appellant Li Shuaishuai was a registered student at a secondary vocational school; therefore, his disability compensation should be calculated based on the per capita disposable income of Shanghai urban residents, amounting to RMB 175,404. The first instance court's application of the standard for Shanghai rural residents was inappropriate, and the second instance corrects this accordingly.

As for lost income, the appellant Li Shuaishuai was a student with no fixed income, and the reduction in income during the post-incident period of lost work was not necessarily equal to his actual income during the short internship period before the incident. The first instance court, referring to the content of the internship agreement, exercised its discretion to calculate lost income at RMB 1,820/month for a period of 6 months, which was not improper. Li Shuaishuai's claim for lost income calculated at RMB 3,000/month lacked sufficient basis and is not adopted by the second instance. In summary, Li Shuaishuai's total economic losses amount to RMB 283,907.51. Of this, 80% amounts to RMB 227,126.01, to be borne by the appellee, General Fuji Company. After deducting the expenses of RMB 78,738.51 advanced by General Fuji Company, General Fuji Company shall actually pay Li Shuaishuai compensation of RMB 148,387.50. The remaining 20% amounts to RMB 56,781.50, to be compensated to Li Shuaishuai by the appellee, Industrial and Commercial School.

In conclusion, in accordance with Article 170, paragraph 1, item (ii) of the *Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China*, Article 6, paragraph 1, Article 12, Article 15, paragraph 1, item (vi), Article 16, Article 22 of the *Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China*, and Article 20, paragraph 3 of the *Regulations of Shanghai Municipality on the Handling of Student Injury Accidents in Primary and Secondary Schools*, the Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on September 7, 2015:

1. Set aside the civil judgment (2015) Qing Min Yi (Min) Chu Zi No. 101 of the Shanghai Qingpu District People's Court;

2. Shanghai General Fuji Refrigeration Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate Li Shuaishuai for his economic losses caused by this injury, in the amount of RMB 148,387.50;

3. Shanghai Industrial and Commercial Information School shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate Li Shuaishuai for his economic losses caused by this injury, in the amount of RMB 56,781.50.

This judgment is final.
